Normal: Free up space soon: Settings > System > Storage (Storage Sense), uninstall unused apps, empty the Recycle Bin.
For finding large files, the open-source WinDirStat is a safe helper.
Bad: Under 10% free: Windows Update can fail and SSDs slow down and wear faster. Free space now via Storage Sense and Disk Cleanup.
Consider moving large media folders to another drive or an external disk.

rules.forecast: An SSD kept nearly full has less room for wear leveling — sustained <10% free measurably accelerates wear.

Bad: BACK UP YOUR IMPORTANT FILES FIRST — before any repair attempt.
The file system reports it needs repair. After backing up, open an admin prompt and run 'chkdsk <drive>: /scan' and follow its guidance.

Normal: TRIM is disabled — SSD performance degrades over time without it. From an admin prompt: 'fsutil behavior set DisableDeleteNotify 0'.
A few disk I/O errors were logged. BACK UP important files as a precaution, then re-scan in a week — growth matters more than the number.
External/USB drives: try a different cable and port first.
Bad: BACK UP YOUR IMPORTANT FILES NOW — repeated disk errors often precede failure.
For SATA drives, reseat or replace the data cable (a $5 fix causes many of these).
Then run the elevated SMART scan (M2) or a vendor diagnostic tool to check the drive itself.

rules.forecast: Disk errors that grow week over week are one of the strongest failure predictors — the safe assumption is that the drive is dying.
